title: Money, not demand, became the AI bottleneck
summary: This week the AI debate moved from *is there demand* to *who pays for it, and at what rate*. With the 10-year at ~5.2%, there were ~$140B of mega-raises and an OpenAI revenue scare. Infrastructure names gained attention but lost sentiment, and the bank cluster jumped from 6% to 20% of briefs. The same yields explain both. The second story is SpaceX: it is pushing into telecom spectrum and compute hosting at once. The telco cluster appeared from nothing (0% to 17%) on negative sentiment.

insights.title: Higher yields turn the AI capex debate into a financing debate
bullets: **Mega-raises:** a Broadcom deal tied to Anthropic (~$40B), SpaceX $40B and others total ~$140B (Paffrath). SpaceX 30-year bonds trade ~15% below par at ~8% yield. Hock Tan: the bottleneck moves 'from memory to money'.

**The OpenAI revenue scare:** a $70B-vs-$50B ARR dispute pulled infrastructure stocks down. Jensen's answer is that labs are only ~25-30% of Nvidia compute, so 'we're putting way too much pressure on two labs'.
**The ai-infra cluster** (Palantir, AMD, Broadcom, Nebius, CoreWeave) rose from 12% to 20% of briefs, but its sentiment slipped from 0.71 to 0.54. Attention is up and conviction is down.

**Bear voices:** Ritholtz says 'back out AI capex and the economy is slightly contracting' and questions A-rated data-center debt. Visser counters that AI debt is asset-backed against compute, and puts 'capital' alone on his watch list.
**Jensen's own fix is financing:** Nvidia invests in neoclouds and takes revenue share. That is vendor financing, the same move Broadcom is making with Anthropic.

insights.title: SpaceX goes after telecom and compute hosting at the same time
bullets: **The telco cluster** (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile) went from 0% to 17% of briefs at -0.24 sentiment. Trigger: Starlink's ~$8B buy of 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management (a new name).
**Market reaction:** T-Mobile ~-13%, AT&T ~-10%, Verizon ~-9%, ASTS -10.5%. Dragu sold all 1,700 ASTS shares and moved into SPCX, AVGO and RKLB.

**Compute hosting:** Herbert counts ~$41.2B a year of SpaceX hosting contracts (Anthropic ~$15B), with 200,000 GB300s online in November. Jensen says xAI now sits in Nvidia's CSP segment and the two are co-designing a server for space.
**Contrarian read:** Jensen describes AT&T and Verizon as reinventing themselves *with* Nvidia. The bear case on telcos assumes they stay pipes.
**Source note:** most of the SpaceX bull case comes from a SpaceX-focused channel and a host who holds 1,000+ SPCX shares.

insights.title: Banks get two different bear stories: an agent derating and a rate trap
bullets: **The bank cluster** (Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citi, Schwab, Wells Fargo) went from 6% to 20% of briefs at ~0.04 sentiment. Stripe/Visa/Mastercard went from 4% to 10%.

**The agent story (Visser):** agents move deposits to the best yield and stablecoins remove settlement float, so he expects a SaaS-style derating within ~9 months (2027-07). Stripe (~$160B, ~10,000 people) versus Citi (~$200B, ~200,000).
**The rate story (Dragu):** Goldman -24%, Capital One -25%, and JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley down 10%+, because a ~5.3% 10-year beats bank dividends and unrealized bond losses build up.
**Tokenization rails:** two new names appeared, Standard Chartered (crypto custody) and Intercontinental Exchange (a tokenized-stock venture with OKX).
**Thin evidence:** the agent derating is mostly one voice (Visser, across his own show and Pompliano's). The rate story is mechanical and would reverse if yields fall.

watch.title: 10-year yield path (5.2-5.3%) and the Anthropic IPO liquidity draw
watch.why: All three stories run through yields: AI financing costs, bank valuations, and long-duration growth names. A reported ~$2T Anthropic listing would also compete with SpaceX and Google for the same liquidity.

watch.title: Powered sites (land/power/shell) versus announced chips
watch.why: Jensen and SemiAnalysis put 2027 at ~43 GW of demand, ~50 GW of announced chips and ~35-40 GW of ready sites. The Samsung/TSMC/SK Hynix supply-chain cluster is emerging (1% to 7%) but rests on only 2 briefs.

watch.title: Efficiency bears versus the scarcity consensus
watch.why: Shkreli (photonic matmul could scrap GPUs; H100s scrapped in 20 years), Ritholtz ('seven-football-field' data centers left empty) and Nadig (orders-of-magnitude inference gains) form a minority view against Jensen and Visser's 'compute stays short'. Attention to it is rising.

watch.title: Open models in the startup layer
watch.why: Jensen says 80% of Nvidia-renting startups use open models. Lambert puts the open-to-frontier lag at 2-3 months, and Meta is rumored to release open weights again. Pricing pressure on closed labs connects back to the financing story.

watch.title: Starlink spectrum approval and telco guidance
watch.why: The ~$8B 800 MHz deal still needs regulatory approval, and the telco re-rating depends on it. This rests on only a handful of briefs, so check the next carrier earnings calls before treating it as a trend.
